pages.title: BotHearth — a self-hosted computer for AI agents
pages.description: Give your AI agent a browser, shell, and workspace on your Mac or Linux machine. Free for permitted noncommercial use, with source, live view, and human control.

pages.title: Install BotHearth on macOS or Linux — quickstart
pages.description: Build BotHearth from source with Node.js 22.18+ and Docker, connect your own model account, and run a small first task you can verify.

pages.title: How BotHearth works — containers, model connections, and MCP
pages.description: Understand the host daemon, separate browser and shell containers, native Codex and Claude Code connections, and BotHearth's task-scoped MCP tools.

pages.title: BotHearth security and privacy — where your data goes
pages.description: Read BotHearth's container, approval, and human-control boundaries; what remote models receive; how task data is retained; and how to report a vulnerability.

pages.title: BotHearth examples — three small tasks with checks
pages.description: Try reproducible browser and workspace tasks in BotHearth. Each example includes a prompt, permissions, expected output, and a way to check the result.

pages.title: BotHearth FAQ — licence, costs, compatibility, and limits
pages.description: Is BotHearth free? What does the usage meter measure? Which platforms work? Clear answers about PolyForm Noncommercial, model costs, and the alpha release.

pages.title: About BotHearth — project, author, and contribution guide
pages.description: BotHearth is maintained by Sanjay Bhat. Explore the source, read the current release boundaries, report reproducible issues, and contribute under the project terms.
